# analysis-video

Produces `context.md`: screens, their images, their time ranges, and the
dialogue spoken during each. That file is what you read.

Generated by analysis-video 0.1.0. Re-run `analysis-video install-skill`
after upgrading if this file ever needs refreshing.

## How to invoke it

Use `analysis-video …` if it is on PATH; otherwise `uvx analysis-video@latest …`
(same thing, no install). Keep the `@latest`: uvx caches the version it resolved
the first time and keeps running that one, so without it you stay pinned to
whatever was current the day this machine first ran the tool. If neither
`analysis-video` nor `uv` exists, tell the user to install uv
(https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and stop — do not try to install anything yourself.

## Start here, every time

1. `analysis-video agent-guide` — **the authoritative usage document.** Run it
   and follow what it says. Every command, flag, default, exit code and output
   path is in there, injected from the real constants. Do not guess flags from
   memory; do not rely on this file for them.
2. `analysis-video status <video>` — where this video stands and what to do
   next. Safe to call on a video that was never analysed. Its `next` field is
   the loop below.

## The loop: keep going until `next.do` is `done`

Analysing a video is **not** finished when `context.md` exists. That file is the
material; the analysis is what you write from it, and this tool keeps a place
for it so it survives the session. Every result carries a `next` object:

- `next.do == "run"` — run `next.command` verbatim, then read the new `next`.
- `next.do == "read"` — open the files in `next.read`, then pipe your analysis
  into `next.command` (it ends in `review --write -`). Write it for a reader who
  has not seen the video.
- `next.do == "done"` — now answer the user.

Stopping at `read` leaves the work unrecorded: the next session finds no
analysis and pays for every image again. `review` is one command; run it.

## Budget: images are the expensive part, not the text

`next.cost` tells you how many images `context.md` points at and roughly what
they cost. Those are already downscaled read copies. If the cost does not fit
your context window:

- **First, open fewer images.** Each entry in `context.md` prints the seconds
  its screen was on display — the long ones carry more.
- **Then re-detect more coarsely** with `--cut-area-threshold` on `analyze`.
  That flag is the one dial that trades images for detail. **Take its default
  and the value to raise it to from `agent-guide`, never from this file** — it
  prints them from the constants the detector actually runs on, and it says what
  the trade costs you. This file is a snapshot of the day it was installed.
- **Never raise `--rate-threshold` to save images — it produces *more*.** That
  value also decides when a screen has settled, so raising it captures earlier,
  busier moments. Raising `--anchor-threshold` is a bad trade too: it saves
  little and drops screens you would have wanted.

Re-detecting rewrites `context.md`, so any review written against the old one is
marked stale and `next` will ask for it again. Decide the threshold before you
read, not after.

An analysis directory is larger than the video it came from, and nothing prunes
it for you. `analysis-video clean <video>` reports what is in there and what can
go; with `--level` it removes it. Your review, the transcript and the reading
copies are never touched by it. Mention this if the user cares about disk.

## Non-negotiables

- **Only the video the user named.** `<video>` is a path to a local file. This
  tool fetches no video and opens no URL. If the file is not on disk, ask for it
  and stop — do not go hunting the filesystem for something that looks close.
- **stdout is one JSON object; branch on the exit code.** stderr is progress
  log for humans — never parse it.
- **Use the paths the JSON gives you.** They are absolute, so you may run from
  any working directory. Read the `context.md` it points at; `metadata.json` is
  an audit record, not something to read end to end.
- **Environment trouble is exit 4.** `analysis-video doctor` diagnoses it and
  takes no arguments. Report its `error.hint` rather than working around it.
  `doctor` lists capabilities and exits 0 whenever the tool can run at all — an
  absent speech-recognition backend is `available: false`, not a fault, because
  a video that carries its own subtitles never needs one.
